readerQuestion: What signal tells a team delegated work has crossed into decision authority?
centralTension: Delegated routine and required judgment can desynchronize when review habits lag behind shifting automation boundaries.
verifiedObservations: Teams sometimes delegate routine coordination to automated assistants before they have a shared rule for when a human must re-enter the loop.
Escalation paths are often defined for failures, but not for ambiguous cases where the assistant has already acted.
inferences: Review habits may lag behind shifting delegation boundaries.
Ambiguous assistant actions may bypass the informal checks teams rely on for judgment-heavy work.
speculation: A lightweight signal may eventually be needed at the workflow layer when delegated actions begin to resemble decisions.
evidenceGaps: Non-blocking uncertainty: keep observation, inference, and speculation separated.
unresolvedQuestions: What lightweight signal would tell a team that a delegated workflow has crossed from assistance into decision authority?
nextAction: Draft bounded field report and preserve uncertainty.
